headline: BOJ Is Said to Keep Rate Hikes on Fast Track, December in Focus
author: Toru Fujioka

paragraphs.text: Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:10 AM MST 2 min read

(Bloomberg) -- The Bank of Japan may maintain a continued fast pace of rate hikes given current price trends and a view at the bank that the impact of increases on the economy so far has been limited, with December the next potential move, according to people familiar with the matter.

Officials at the bank see the underlying inflation trend as having reached a level broadly consistent with the BOJ's target of 2%, these people said. However, they added, the officials feel the current policy rate still appears some distance from a neutral rate — one that neither stimulates nor restrains the economy.

Against that backdrop, the BOJ sees an increasing need to stabilize underlying inflation around its target level, according to these people. The recently accelerated pace of rate hikes could more or less continue as long as the economy and inflation develop in line with the BOJ's view, the people said.

These people stress that there is no predetermined path for borrowing costs, with decisions depending on the economic outlook, risks surrounding it and the cumulative impact of rate increases so far. However, they say the BOJ sees no urgency to raise rates immediately after last month's move. Another increase is as possible as early as December, the people said.

The BOJ raised its benchmark rate for the second time in three months in September — the fastest pace of rate hikes since 1990. Views among BOJ officials point to a possibility that the bank will roughly maintain the same pace by tightening borrowing every quarter.

The BOJ is widely expected to stand pat at a policy meeting ending on Oct 30. The bank will issue a new quarterly economic outlook after the meeting, but no major changes are expected beyond some tweaks in its projections for economic growth and inflation, according to the people.
On Friday, data showed the consumer price index excluding fresh food — one of the BOJ's main measures of inflation — rose 2.1% in September, the first time it has exceeded the BOJ's target this year.

People familiar with the matter earlier told Bloomberg that the BOJ is likely to indicate at the policy meeting next week that underlying inflation has reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was set in 2013.
